branch: stream_event/message_start usage -> setContext -> the .ctx chip's ring
provenance: The driver is measured: `message_start` carries the prompt-side usage and is the only live feed into setContext (chat.html sums input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens). Nothing here asserts an absolute percentage, and that is deliberate rather than lazy: the harness drives a panel with a REAL CLI attached, whose own model events set ctxWindowFromCli whenever they arrive, so the same usage renders 24% against a 200k window and 5% against a 1M one — measured mid-run, a first draft of this fixture failed exactly that way. What is pinned instead is what the ring must satisfy for ANY window: the arc equals the digits, the threshold agrees with both, and the ring survives an update — the previous code wrote `textContent`, which would delete the <svg> on the first refresh.

steps.note: first usage draws the ring and the number together

expect.why: the .gauge gate is on, so chat.css actually draws it

expect.js: (() => { const c = document.getElementById('ctxChip'); return c.style.getPropertyValue('--ctx-pct') + '%' === c.lastChild.nodeValue; })()
expect.why: the arc is driven by the same number the digits show

expect.js: (() => { const c = document.getElementById('ctxChip'); const p = +c.style.getPropertyValue('--ctx-pct'); return c.classList.contains('warn') === (p >= 50); })()
expect.why: the threshold agrees with the figure, whatever the window turned out to be
the dash array is a percentage only because the path is 100 units long
the usage side IS deterministic — 1k + 47k — even when the window is not

steps.note: a heavier turn updates BOTH, and the ring survives it — the regression this fixture exists for

expect.why: still exactly one ring: not deleted by the update, not duplicated by it

expect.js: (() => { const c = document.getElementById('ctxChip'); return c.style.getPropertyValue('--ctx-pct') + '%' === c.lastChild.nodeValue; })()
expect.why: arc still equals digits after a re-render

expect.js: (() => { const c = document.getElementById('ctxChip'); const p = +c.style.getPropertyValue('--ctx-pct'); return c.classList.contains('warn') === (p >= 50); })()
expect.why: and the threshold still agrees — the ring turns with the text, both being currentColor

steps.note: NEGATIVE CONTROL — the ring is geometry copied from the composer's Lucide icons, so it must MEASURE like one

expect.why: the same 13.5px the square-slash's rect measures: r=9 in a 24 viewBox spans units 3..21, exactly like <rect x=3 width=18>

expect.js: (() => { const a = document.querySelector('#ctxChip .ctx-ring').getBoundingClientRect(); const b = document.querySelectorAll('#inputbar .icon-btn')[1].querySelector('svg').getBoundingClientRect(); return Math.round(a.width) === Math.round(b.width); })()
expect.why: same box as the slash icon beside it, so the two glyphs sit on one rhythm

steps.note: a new conversation leaves nothing stale behind — __clear is the path that zeroes the gauge, setContext(0) returns early by design

expect.why: the arc is cleared too — otherwise the next first render flashes the previous session's fill
and the digits are blanked without taking the ring with them
the ring is still there, ready for the next session
